title: Dell Revenue Doubles to $54.9 Billion as AI Server Sales Nearly Quadruple
yt_title: Dell Just Had Its Biggest Quarter Ever: $54.9B, AI Servers Up 291%
yt_description:
Dell's revenue more than doubled to a record $54.9 billion as AI server sales hit $22 billion, almost four times more than a year ago. Its AI backlog reached a record $132.3 billion, and Dell raised its full-year forecast to $202 billion, plus a new $25 billion buyback. But PCs grew only 3%, and a memory chip shortage is expected to last into 2027.

script: Welcome to IT News, AI News! Dell just had the biggest quarter in its history. Revenue hit fifty four point nine billion dollars. That's up one hundred and three percent in one year! Wall Street expected about forty nine billion. Dell beat that by more than five billion. The rocket fuel? AI servers. They brought in twenty two billion dollars, almost four times more than a year ago. Dell's server and storage group nearly tripled, to almost forty two billion. And the order book is wild. Sixty billion dollars of new AI orders, in just three months. That pushes Dell's AI backlog to a record one hundred thirty two billion dollars. More than seven thousand five hundred customers are now building Dell AI factories. Profit jumped too. Adjusted earnings hit nine dollars forty five per share, versus six fifty nine expected. But PCs? Much calmer. The PC business grew only three percent, and consumer sales fell fifteen percent. Dell raised its forecast for the third time this year. Full year revenue: two hundred two billion dollars. AI servers alone should bring in seventy eight billion this year. One catch: Dell expects the memory chip shortage to last into twenty twenty seven. Shareholders get another twenty five billion dollars for buybacks. The stock jumped about five percent after hours. Bottom line: the AI gold rush needs shovels, and Dell is selling a mountain of them. Read the full story on itnewsainews dot xpigeon dot net. See you next time!
